proposal.utterance: Recognition can fail to occur, leaving an obligation ungrounded.

entities.label: RecognitionFailure
entities.rationale: A recognition failure is an occurrent — a happening (or non-happening) that unfolds in time. Modeling it as a Process subclass captures the idea that the act of social recognition (already in the ontology as SocialRecognition: BFO_0000015) may fail to occur; the failure is itself a process-type event (an absent or abortive process). This parallels how BFO handles process boundaries and absences.

entities.label: UngroundedObligation
entities.rationale: An ungrounded obligation is a subtype of LegalObligation (Role, BFO_0000023) that lacks the social recognition grounding that would normally confer it. It still inheres in a bearer as a role, but its grounding condition (SocialRecognition) has not been realized. Modeling it as a subclass of the existing LegalObligation preserves the typing while adding the qualification.

entities.label: RecognitionGroundingCondition
entities.rationale: The statement implies that recognition normally grounds an obligation — i.e., there is a grounding condition (a disposition) that, when realized through a SocialRecognition process, results in a properly grounded LegalObligation. This is best typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016), internally grounded in the institution or norm-bearer, that is realized in recognition processes.

relations.rationale: RecognitionFailure is a Process subclass — a type of occurrent event (the absence or failure of a recognition process).
An ungrounded obligation is a species of LegalObligation, distinguished by lacking its required grounding via recognition.
The grounding condition is a disposition that is normally realized in a SocialRecognition process.
The recognition grounding condition is realized in (BFO_0000054) a SocialRecognition process when recognition successfully occurs.

RecognitionFailure is a subclass of SocialRecognition in the sense that it is a degenerate or null case of the recognition process — the attempted or expected recognition process that does not complete. This keeps the two classes related under a common parent while distinguishing successful from failed recognition.

open_questions: Should RecognitionFailure be modeled as a proper subclass of SocialRecognition (a failed/abortive process) or as a distinct Process class that stands in contrast to SocialRecognition? BFO does not have native absence-of-process classes, so this choice affects reasoning.

Is 'ungrounded obligation' meant to denote an obligation that never becomes valid (a mere purported obligation), or one that was once grounded but whose grounding has lapsed? This affects whether UngroundedObligation should be disjoint from properly grounded LegalObligation or merely a phase of it.

Should RecognitionGroundingCondition inhere specifically in LegalInstitution individuals, in norm-bearers, or in LegalObligation instances themselves? Clarifying the bearer is needed to complete the RO_0000052 (inheres in) assertion.

Does 'leaving an obligation ungrounded' mean the obligation fails to exist, or that it exists as a purported role without proper institutional backing? This bears on whether UngroundedObligation individuals have a bearer at all in BFO terms.

entities.label: PropertyStatus

It is externally grounded in recognition practices, making Role the appropriate BFO typing. It is distinct from a mere quality because it depends on ongoing social/institutional recognition rather than intrinsic features of the bearer.

entities.label: RecognitionConditionOperation

Modeling it as a Process captures the dynamic, time-unfolding nature of that operation, distinct from the condition (Disposition) itself.

entities.label: PropertyStatusDependenceOnRecognitionThesis
entities.rationale: The claim that property status depends on the continued operation of a recognition condition is a propositional/theoretical content—an information artifact that can be encoded, copied, and discussed. It belongs with other thesis-individuals already in the ontology (e.g. CollectiveMaintenanceExistenceThesis, OntologicalValidityThesis).

relations.rationale: PropertyStatus is a subclass of Role (BFO_0000023), as it is an externally grounded, socially recognised status inhering in a bearer.
RecognitionConditionOperation is a subclass of Process, representing the ongoing exercise/operation of a recognition condition over time.
An operation of a recognition condition realizes the LegalExistenceCondition (a Disposition): the process realizes the disposition it instantiates.
PropertyStatus (as a Role/realizable) is realized in the RecognitionConditionOperation process, capturing the dependence of property status on the continued operation of a recognition condition.
The thesis is an individual generically dependent continuant, consistent with other thesis individuals in the ontology.

open_questions: Is 'property status' here specifically legal property ownership (a right to possess/use/transfer), or does it also cover other kinds of status (e.g. corporate personhood, citizenship)? This affects whether PropertyStatus should be a subclass of LegalRight rather than directly of Role.

Should RecognitionConditionOperation be modeled as realizing LegalLegitimacyCondition, LegalExistenceCondition, or both? The utterance is ambiguous about which kind of condition grounds property status.

Should PropertyStatusDependenceOnRecognitionThesis be linked to an existing individual such as CollectiveMaintenanceExistenceThesis or RecognitionOriginThesis via a 'part of' or entailment relation?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a dependency relation: property status (a socially conferred role) exists only so long as a recognition condition continues to operate. Three ontological commitments are extracted: (1) PropertyStatus as a Role class (BFO_0000023), externally grounded in recognition—distinct from a mere quality because its existence is contingent on ongoing social/institutional activity rather than intrinsic bearer properties; (2) RecognitionConditionOperation as a Process class (BFO_0000015) capturing the temporally extended, ongoing exercise of a recognition condition—this complements the existing LegalExistenceCondition and LegalLegitimacyCondition Disposition classes by representing their active instantiation; (3) PropertyStatusDependenceOnRecognitionThesis as an individual generically dependent continuant, consistent with the many thesis-individuals already in the ontology. The key relational commitment is that PropertyStatus is realized in RecognitionConditionOperation (BFO_0000054/BFO_0000055), formalizing the claimed dependence. Several open questions remain about scope and the precise kind of recognition condition involved.
